item.title: Orcas Are Hunting Great White Sharks for One Organ — And It's Changing the Ocean
item.description:
Off the coast of South Africa, something happened that shouldn't have been possible: great white sharks, the ocean's most feared predator, started disappearing from a bay they'd dominated for decades.
The cause wasn't disease, overfishing, or warming water. It was two orcas — nicknamed Port and Starboard — hunting great whites for a single organ: the liver. Rich in squalene and critical for buoyancy, a shark's liver is a calorie-dense meal the orcas have learned to extract with surgical precision, sometimes in under two minutes.
In this episode, we break down the real research behind this behavior, how it's documented to be displacing great white populations entirely from areas they once dominated, and what researchers believe this could mean for the wider ecosystem as mid-level predators move in to fill the gap.
